title: Anna, eighty-four (Luke 2:36–40)
hook: a widow who never left the temple speaks of the child to all who waited

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Nunc dimittis: Simeon held the child and was ready to go off duty. Your line was depart in peace. What good thing had your eyes seen by bedtime? Day five hundred eleven.

Some congregations have a woman like this. She's been there longer than anyone. She knows where the spare candles are kept. She was praying in that pew before the current pastor was born. She's buried a husband, maybe more than one friend, and she keeps coming, early, every time the doors open. Visitors walk right past her. And she's often the one who notices when something real is happening. Luke has just told us about Simeon. Now, in the same temple, in that same instant, he introduces her ancient counterpart, in three short verses.

In the King James Bible: "And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser." Aser is Asher, one of the tribes of Israel. And Anna is the Greek form of Hannah, the same name as the Hannah whose song echoed in Mary's. Luke tells us she was married only seven years, and then: "she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day." Fourscore and four is eighty-four. And here's the puzzle: even in English, the line can be read two ways. She was eighty-four years old, or she'd been a widow for eighty-four years, which would make her far older. Translations differ. Either way, years of the same faithful routine, in the same place, waiting. Then: "she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem." That instant. After all those years, her timing is perfect. And look what she does. Simeon sings and blesses. Anna talks. She goes around telling everyone who's been waiting like her. In a way she's one of the first people in Luke to tell others about Jesus. Some readers notice Luke pairing a man and a woman: Zechariah and Mary, Simeon and Anna. Then the family goes home to Nazareth, and the child grows strong, filled with wisdom, the grace of God upon him. This week has been crowded with people waiting: Mary's yes, Mary's song, Zechariah's Benedictus, the census, the shepherds, Simeon. And Anna, who never stopped.
screen: `OF THE TRIBE OF ASER, OR ASHER.`
then, large: `SHE DEPARTED NOT FROM THE TEMPLE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: thank an old woman of faith. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind an older woman whose faithfulness shaped you, or someone near you. A grandmother who prayed for you. A neighbor who always asked how you were. A teacher, a nun, an aunt, the woman at church who remembered your name. She doesn't have to share your beliefs; she just has to be someone who kept showing up. Picture her face, her hands, the place you'd usually find her. Let yourself be grateful for the years she gave. If you pray, you can give thanks for her by name. If you don't, simply hold her in gratitude, and decide how you'll tell her, or how you'll honor her memory. The bell holds the time.
Anna. A prophetess, widowed young, who prayed in the temple night and day for years, and told everyone who was waiting about the child.
Your line: she never stopped. Today, call, write or visit an older woman of faith and thank her, specifically, for one thing. Day five hundred eleven, and another week on the path.

howItsDone: Anna is remembered with Simeon at the feast of the Presentation on February 2 in some churches, and Orthodox and Catholic Christians honor her as a saint.

match.prompt: what's inside Luke 2:36–40 — tap the pairs.
pairs: spoke of him to all who waited

myth: Luke clearly says Anna was eighty-four years old
the line can mean she was eighty-four, or that she had been a widow for eighty-four years.
Anna was married only seven years
Luke says she lived with a husband seven years, and then was widowed.
Anna was from the tribe of Judah
she was from the tribe of Aser, or Asher.

fork.setup: you're Anna. you've prayed in the temple night and day for years, and you've just seen the child Simeon is holding. what do you do?
options: go quietly back to your prayers.
give thanks, and tell everyone who's been waiting.
ask the parents to stay in Jerusalem.
fork.reveal: she gives thanks and "spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem." Simeon sings; Anna tells.

original.note: Hebrew: Hannah, the name of Samuel's mother. Anna is its Greek form.

trapdoor: what you thought: an old lady who happened to be in the temple.
what it means: a prophetess who prayed night and day for years recognizes the child in that instant and tells everyone who was waiting.
what a scholar hears: she's from the tribe of Asher, her name is Hannah's, and the line leaves her age unclear: eighty-four, or eighty-four years a widow.
recall: friend of God, or loved by God

sources.quoted: And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser
she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.

notes: The index title says 'eighty-four'; Luke 2:37's Greek is ambiguous between age 84 and 84 years of widowhood. Both are given.

Asher as one of the northern tribes many thought lost after the Assyrian conquest; some members are recorded remaining (2 Chronicles 30:11). Reviewer edit: softened to 'often spoken of as lost after the Assyrian conquest'. Confirm wording.
'One of the first people in Luke to tell others about Jesus' — the shepherds also told others (2:17). Phrased as 'one of the first'.
Luke's male/female pairing is a common scholarly observation. Confirm.
The temple scene does not say the parents stayed or left immediately; 2:39 says they returned to Nazareth after performing everything.
